label: Cosmic Web
caption: Galaxies trace a cosmic web: filaments of matter wrapped around vast empty voids.
credit: FLAMINGO project / Virgo Consortium (Schaye et al. 2023, MNRAS 526, 4978)
notes: Background of Fig. 1 of Schaye et al. 2023 (open-access MNRAS, CC BY 4.0; file images/SEC0IMG8_full.png, 2100 px): 40 Mpc-thick slice of the full 2.8 Gpc box at z=0 (CDM brightness, neutrino density as colour). The 2100 px image spans the full 2.8 Gpc (checked against the 1 Gpc bar in Fig. 1: 457/1280 px). Cropped 8 px per side to remove a blue edge line, so 2084 px = 2778.7 Mpc. A hue-preserving luminance black point (27th percentile, gamma 1.3) turns the blue void fog black. About 1/10 the diameter of the observable universe, so it is labelled 'Cosmic Web'. Focus = bright yellow cluster node near the centre. The website gives no explicit licence; CC BY 4.0 comes from the published figure.

label: Cosmic Filaments
caption: Gas streams along filaments into galaxy clusters, the densest knots of the cosmic web.
license: Free to share with credit ('TNG Collaboration'); non-commercial; commercial use requires contacting the TNG team
notes: OPTIONAL BRIDGE LEVEL (not in the original list) that splits the x56 jump from cosmic-web to supercluster. The file is boxImage_TNG300-1_gas-coldens_thinSlice_2000.png: gas column density in a 100 kpc thin slice across the full TNG300-1 box (205 cMpc/h = 302.6 Mpc) at z=0, centred on the most massive cluster. No crop. The constant navy floor (6,14,19) was subtracted per channel. Focus = the central massive cluster.

label: Supercluster
caption: Every speck is a galaxy, strung along filaments spanning 160 million light-years.
license: Free to share with credit ('TNG Collaboration'); non-commercial; commercial use requires contacting the TNG team
notes: boxImage_TNG100-1_stars-coldens_3840.png: stellar mass column density (stars only), described as 'a 50 Mpc region', z=0. width_m assumes the 50 Mpc is the horizontal width (3840 px). Cluster ICL sizes (~2 Mpc) support this, but it is not confirmed and could be about ±10%. The background is already pure black (the grey+alpha PNG was composited onto black). No crop. Focus = the most massive cluster (large ICL blob, left of centre).

label: Galaxy Cluster
caption: A galaxy cluster: hundreds of galaxies held by 200 trillion Suns' worth of mass.
credit: D. Nelson, G. Joshi / IllustrisTNG Collaboration (TNG50-1)
license: Free to share with credit ('TNG Collaboration'); non-commercial; commercial use requires contacting the TNG team
notes: OPTIONAL BRIDGE LEVEL (not in the original list) that splits the ~x300 jump from supercluster to galaxy-group. It is the left panel (1920x1920) of TNG50_z0_2clusters_stars_4k.png: stellar light of the most massive TNG50 halo (log M = 14.3) at z=0. Two virial-radius circles and the corner text/scale bar were removed with OpenCV Telea inpainting. Scale: the 300 kpc bar was 242 px, so 1920 px = 2.380 Mpc. A gentle luminance black point was applied (8th percentile, gamma 1.1). The diffuse grey glow is real intracluster light. Focus = a bright satellite galaxy with close neighbours, lower right.

label: Galaxy Group
caption: Stephan's Quintet: a group of galaxies colliding 290 million light-years away.
notes: JWST NIRCam+MIRI mosaic weic2208a (12654x12132 original, 6.34 x 6.08 arcmin), resized to 4096 px wide. width_m = 6.34 arcmin at 290 Mly, the distance of the interacting members. NGC 7320 (left) is a foreground galaxy at 40 Mly, so the scale does not apply to it. Per-channel black point at the sky level (12,11,10). Contains foreground stars with JWST diffraction spikes. Focus = nucleus of NGC 7319, the barred spiral at the top of the group.

label: Milky Way
caption: Our galaxy is over 100,000 light-years across and holds some 100–400 billion stars.
notes: Swapped in for the R. Hurt concept (blotchy when magnified). Sun located by fitting the distance rings of the labelled twin: centre (2500,3518)/5000; rings = 5/10/20 kpc at 127.2 px/kpc (Sun-GC 1037 px = 8.15 kpc) -> width 1.2126e21 m.

label: The Moon
caption: The Moon is 3,474 km across, about a quarter as wide as Earth.
notes: Full Moon photo from 2010-10-22 (Celestron 9.25 SCT, 20 stacked frames), original 2580x2452. Cropped to a 2400x2400 square with the disk centred (disk centre at 0.5002, 0.4998). A least-squares circle fit to the limb (threshold 30/255) gives a disk diameter of 2140.4 px (thresholds 15 and 60 give 2143.5 and 2138.3 px), so width_m = 3.4748e6 m x 2400 / 2140.4. Background already pure black (0). No resampling. ShareAlike applies to derivatives.
